description: Barocal is replacing harmful refrigerants with high-efficiency solid-state cooling technology for the $500B global HVAC market. Cambridge-based Barocal is commercialising solid-state cooling using barocaloric materials, a breakthrough resulting from 15 years of research at the University of Cambridge. Instead of cycling high-GWP refrigerant gases like conventional systems, Barocal’s technology applies pressure to proprietary solid-state barocaloric materials to transfer heat. This eliminates refrigerant leakage and the emissions associated with it. Why we invested in Barocal The climate case : Cooling emits over 4 Gt CO₂e annually, accounting for more than 7% of global greenhouse gas emissions, which makes it one of the largest decarbonisation blind spots. These emissions come from HFC refrigerant leakage, which often have global warming potentials more than 1,000 times higher than CO₂, as well as from the energy intensity of cooling itself. Cooling demand is projected to triple by 2050 , further increasing these emissions. Barocal directly addresses both leakage and energy consumption by eliminating refrigerant gases entirely and delivering significantly higher efficiency than existing solutions. The business case : The global HVAC market is worth approximately $450 billion and is expected to grow to $577 billion by 2033. Barocal is initially focused on commercial chillers and data centre cooling, targeting some of the fastest-growing and most profitable segments. The company is working in collaboration with large OEMs to bring the technology to market. In addition to the emissions benefits, higher efficiency reduces energy costs and results in a lower total cost of ownership for customers. The team : Prof. Xavier Moya, Co-Founder and CEO, is a Professor of Materials Physics at the University of Cambridge and a globally recognised pioneer in caloric materials and barocalorics. He has authored more than 150 scientific publications with over 15,000 citations. He founded Barocal to commercialise his breakthrough research, funded by the Royal Society and the European Research Council. Dr. Giles Rodway, Co-Founder and CTO, brings decades of industrial R&D experience from the automotive sector and previously founded Spinetic, combining deep engineering expertise with proven entrepreneurial credibility. Website: https://barocal.com/ Founded 2019 Management Prof. Xavier Moya Dr. Giles Rodway Location Cambridge, UK Segment Industry World Fund Investment Stage

description: enerkii is slashing industrial energy bills while decarbonising one of Europe’s hardest-to-abate sectors. The Munich-based company provides a full-service, emissions-free energy system for industrial and commercial players across Europe. By combining software intelligence with on-site renewable infrastructure, enerkii enables companies to cut their energy bills by up to 50%, with zero upfront investment. Through its unique “Energy-as-a-Service” model, enerkii is eliminating the complexity, risk, and cost of industrial decarbonisation. Why we invested in enerkii The climate case: Energy production accounts for ~75% of global CO₂ emissions, and industrial energy use remains one of the slowest sectors to decarbonise. Over 80% of industrial sites in Germany still rely on fossil fuels despite increasing renewable availability. enerkii directly addresses this by enabling affordable, zero-emission on-site energy generation. With 87 MW of contracted capacity already secured, enerkii is on track to reduce industrial emissions at scale - just as Germany and the EU accelerate towards 2030 renewable energy targets. The business case: enerkii unlocks an enormous untapped market: the decarbonisation of Europe’s commercial and industrial sectors. While competitors focus on point solutions, enerkii offers a fully integrated system, including solar, battery storage, charging infrastructure, and (soon) heat pumps. These assets are backed by a proprietary Operating System (OS) that configures optimal setups in minutes. Their business model is elegant and compelling: no investment, no complexity, just savings. enerkii already has 18 contracts with major German industrial players, and is well-positioned for Europe-wide expansion. The team: Co-founder and CEO David Balensiefen is a serial entrepreneur who previously co-founded gridX, which he successfully exited to E.ON. He is joined by gridX veterans Henry Thierhoff and Hendrik Abel, forming a team with deep technical knowledge, proven operational execution, and a bold vision for building Europe’s next major decentralised energy provider. description: HYPERSCALE POWER IS BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF ELECTRIC POWER INFRASTRUCTURE. The Zurich-based deeptech company is developing compact solid-state transformers (SSTs) designed for the power demands of AI data centres, EV charging, and large-scale renewable energy systems. Hyperscale Power’s proprietary design is roughly 10× smaller than conventional transformers and uses around 90% less material, dramatically reducing deployment timelines from years to weeks. By leveraging high-frequency operation and advanced power electronics, the system achieves energy-conversion efficiencies of up to 98.5% – significantly higher than today’s solutions. With a clear efficiency, cost, and emissions advantage, Hyperscale Power is positioned to unlock faster electrification and power delivery for the infrastructure underpinning the next industrial era. Why we invested in Hyperscale Power The climate case: Electricity systems lose around 6–8% of generated power globally through transmission and conversion inefficiencies. At the same time, the rapid growth of AI compute, EV charging networks, and renewable power generation is dramatically increasing electricity demand. Hyperscale Power’s solid-state transformers offer up to 98.5% energy-conversion efficiency and enable more flexible, modular grid architectures that can integrate renewables more effectively. Even a 2% improvement in efficiency at hyperscale data-centre and grid level translates into millions of tonnes of avoided CO₂ emissions. The company’s compact design also reduces material usage by roughly 90%, lowering embodied emissions and supporting a more resource-efficient power infrastructure. The business case: Hyperscale Power is entering a rapidly expanding multi-billion-euro market driven by hyperscalers, electrification, and global investment in energy infrastructure. Transformer supply chains are currently strained, with lead times stretching to 18–24 months as demand for high-power systems accelerates. Hyperscale Power’s SST technology dramatically shortens deployment timelines while delivering higher efficiency and power density. This creates a compelling value proposition for data centres, EV charging networks, and renewable-energy operators that need faster, more efficient power conversion to meet growing electricity demands. The team: Hyperscale Power was founded in 2025 by Daniel Rothmund and Sami Pettersson, who each bring more than a decade of experience in solid-state transformers and medium-voltage high-power converters. Their deep technical expertise in power electronics and transformer architecture underpins the company’s proprietary design. Based in Zurich, the team benefits from close ties to Europe’s leading engineering ecosystem around ETH Zürich, positioning the company to attract top technical talent and rapidly bring its technology to market. description: Lithosquare is accelerating critical minerals discovery with AI-driven geological intelligence that addresses the global supply bottleneck. The Paris-based company helps mining companies identify, rank and advance high-potential copper, lithium and rare earth deposits, faster, with higher confidence and at a fraction of the traditional cost. What sets Lithosquare apart is its geology-first approach. Where most AI-exploration tools look for statistical patterns in historical data, Lithosquare reasons from the science of how deposits form. Its platform is built around a proprietary metallogeny ontology covering around 20 deposit types, developed and maintained by PhD metallogenists working alongside AI engineers. This allows the system to generate credible targets in greenfield areas where no historical training data exists, a capability that pattern matching approaches cannot replicate. Why we invested in Lithosquare The climate case: Only around 1 in 1,000 mineral exploration projects ever becomes a mine, yet global demand for copper, lithium and rare earths is accelerating as electrification and AI infrastructure intensify. Average mine development lead times have stretched to nearly 18 years, creating a critical gap between exploration decisions today and production needed in the 2030s and 2040s. Lithosquare directly addresses this bottleneck by accelerating high-confidence discovery in jurisdictions that can meet Western supply-chain resilience requirements. By bringing new reserves to market faster and from jurisdictions with stronger environmental standards, Lithosquare unblocks the materials supply that global electrification depends on. The business case: Global mineral exploration budgets have historically ranged between $12-15bn annually, with a portion allocated to target generation, data analytics and technical advisory. Lithosquare's asset-light, partnership-driven model captures exploration service revenues while retaining long-term economic upside through Net Smelter Return royalties on successful discoveries. The global royalty and streaming sector has a combined enterprise value of over $140bn. Early partnerships validate strong demand for AI-accelerated exploration workflows and demonstrate traction across both large-cap operators and mid-tier explorers. The team: Co-Founder and CEO Aymeric Preveral-Etcheverry previously scaled Fieldbox, an industrial AI company. COO Simon Leclair brings 15+ years of mining expertise, including early-career mine development work at Eramet and 8 years as a partner at BCG specialising in Metals and Mining strategy. Both are Mines Paris graduates, combining deep geological credibility with proven operational execution and AI expertise. Website: https://www.lithosquare.com/ Founded 2024 Management Aymeric Preveral-Etcheverry, Co-Founder & CEO Simon Leclair, Founding COO Location Paris, France Segment Industry / Critical Materials World Fund Investment Stage

description: Nitricity is electrifying organic fertilizer production with a world-first, plant-based alternative that’s transforming agriculture. The US-based company has developed Ash Tea , a liquid organic nitrogen fertilizer made from recycled almond shells, air, water, and renewable energy. Fully vegan, pathogen-free, and cost-competitive, Ash Tea is already sold out for years to come, with farmers lining up to secure supply. With its first commercial-scale facility breaking ground in Delhi, California, Nitricity is scaling globally to meet surging demand from organic growers in the US and Europe. Why we invested in Nitricity The climate case: Conventional fertilizers made through the Haber-Bosch process are responsible for ~2% of global GHG emissions, while also degrading soils, polluting waterways, and driving biodiversity loss. Worse, up to 70% of nitrogen applied is lost to the environment 1 . Nitricity’s organic, circular alternative cuts emissions by more than 90% and restores soil health, while replacing animal-based fertilizers with a cleaner, safer option. By producing nitrogen fertilizer from agricultural waste and renewable energy, Nitricity directly addresses one of agriculture’s most urgent decarbonisation challenges. The business case: Nitricity is addressing the $150B global fertilizer market, starting with a beachhead in organic nitrogen fertilizer for high-value crops, a segment worth over $11B on its own 2 . Farmers are eager for better, affordable solutions, and Nitricity delivers. Its product flows seamlessly through irrigation systems, avoids clogging, and enables more efficient nitrogen use, cutting input costs. With over $150m already in its sales pipeline and binding offtake agreements stretching through 2028, Nitricity is scaling from proven demand, not speculative adoption. The company’s Series B raise, closed in the third quarter of 2025, will accelerate US expansion, advance R&D, and build the European customer pipeline and partnerships in preparation for international growth. The team: Founded in 2018 by Stanford graduates Dr. Nicolas Pinkowski (CEO), Dr. Joshua McEnaney (President & CTO), and Dr. Jay Schwalbe (CSO), Nitricity began with a solar-powered experiment on a lemon tree. Today, the founders lead a 38-person team with deep scientific expertise, a clear commercial track record, and a bold vision for circular, plant-based fertilizer production. Their entrepreneurial grit, coupled with strategic backing from leading climate and agri-tech investors, positions Nitricity as a future global leader in sustainable fertilizer. description: Net Zero Nitrogen (NZN) is pioneering a new generation of sustainable agriculture with its breakthrough biofertilizer solution. The UK-based agtech company is developing a novel bioinoculant using naturally occurring endophytic bacteria that colonize crops to reduce the need for synthetic nitrogen fertilizers (SNFs). Unlike most alternatives, NZN’s solution is non-GM, requires no new machinery, and is easy to apply. It offers farmers a “green discount”: lower costs with higher yields and reduced emissions. NZN has already shown strong traction in ASEAN, where it is preparing to scale with the support of major climate-focused investors. Why we invested in NZN The climate case: Synthetic nitrogen fertilizers are responsible for ~2% of global GHG emissions (1.13 Gt CO₂e) and are a leading source of nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas nearly 300 times more potent than CO₂. The production and overuse of SNFs also damages soil microbiomes, pollutes waterways, and drives biodiversity loss. NZN’s bioinoculant technology delivers up to 88% fewer emissions during production and mitigates downstream pollution. This makes it a powerful lever for climate mitigation in agriculture, a sector often overlooked in decarbonisation. The business case: NZN is entering a $200B global fertilizer market with a solution that’s both more sustainable and more cost-effective. The product requires no regulatory exemptions, no GM approval, and no farmer behavior change. It’s already generating significant traction in ASEAN markets through multiple proof-of-concept trials and interest from major agri-input distributors. With minimal transmission loss and no nitrous oxide leakage, NZN offers not just a green premium, but a green discount. The team: CEO Justin Hughes brings entrepreneurial vision and leadership experience as a former Red Arrows pilot, while CSO Dr. Gary Devine leads scientific development with deep biological expertise. Together with co-founder Alan Burbidge, the NZN team combines scientific rigour and strategic execution, positioning the company to transform one of agriculture’s most polluting inputs. description: Planet A Foods is a food-tech company that developed a technology platform to create a socially-just and environmentally-friendly food industry. They develop sustainable, future-oriented products free from any highly-limited resources such as cocoa or palm oil. All items are created from solely natural ingredients - with the first use case being cacao butter & cacao powder. Why we invested: The climate case : Chocolate production comes at a high cost for the planet. The rising demand for cocoa is a major driver for the deforestation in tropical forests, which are some of the most important carbon sinks on our planet. Climate change itself - and the broader biodiversity crisis - is also threatening the viability of producing cocoa. The business case : the great barrier for any food-tech business is the taste test. Planet A Foods’ Nocoa product offers a nearly identical taste and texture to conventionally produced chocolate - because of its fermentation approach - the best on the market we have tried. The team : CEO Maximilian has previously founded 27Pilots, a boutique consultancy helping startups secure venture funding. Prior he also worked in the automobile industry for half a decade. CTO Sara was a researcher at the Technical University of Munich, analysing the molecular structure of coffee, before working as Principal Scientist at Atomo Coffee, and as Head of Flavour at the Zurich University of Applied Sciences. description: QuantumDiamonds accelerates semiconductor development, improves production yields, and is poised to become the only startup to win manufacturing funding under the European Chips Act. Quantum Diamonds Sensor Technology (QDST) is redefining chip testing with world-first quantum sensing tools that detect hidden defects in complex semiconductors. The Munich-based company enables manufacturers to identify faults in 3D chip architectures before energy- and water-intensive processing steps, reducing waste and emissions. QDST’s platform provides non-destructive, nanometer-scale current imaging, pushing the boundaries of semiconductor metrology. Already working with global chip leaders, QDST is scaling manufacturing with support from the European Chips Act to meet soaring demand for high-yield, high-performance chips. The climate case: The semiconductor industry’s energy use has surged by 125% in recent years, with yield losses causing unnecessary energy, water, and material consumption. QDST’s breakthrough testing tools catch defects early, improving yields and cutting emissions by over 5% through yield optimisation. Additional emissions savings are expected from battery-yield optimisation, as well as from the indirect effects of accelerated EV adoption and enhanced computing efficiency. At scale, these combined effects will drive significant CO2 reductions across critical industries, directly supporting global decarbonisation efforts. The business case: As chips become denser and more complex, today’s tools fall short. QDST is entering a €20B market with a unique solution that solves a growing industry bottleneck. Its quantum sensing system enables accurate, fast, and non-destructive testing of advanced chips, critical for AI, HPC, and EV technologies. Already used by leading global chipmakers, QDST is now scaling production and deployments to become the new testing standard in semiconductor fabs worldwide. The team: Co-founders Kevin Berghoff, Dr. Fleming Bruckmaier, and Prof. Dr. Dominik Bucher lead a world-class team of physicists, engineers, and software developers from TUM, ETH Zurich, LMU, and Harvard. With backing from semiconductor veterans with decades of experience at ASML, Intel, TSMC, and Applied Materials, QDST combines deep technical excellence with strategic industry insight. Space Forge is on a mission to lead the next industrial revolution by harnessing space. The UK-based startup is developing a fully returnable satellite platform designed for manufacturing superior materials in orbit to enable large-scale emissions reduction on Earth. These satellites will leverage a zero-gravity, zero-pollution production environment- with high-efficiency semiconductors as one of its first use cases Why we invested: The climate case : global IT energy use to hit 20% of global emissions by 2030. Space Forge’s in-space manufactured semiconductors can reduce energy usage by 75% - by harnessing unique space conditions of microgravity, vacuum and low temperatures. The business case : semiconductor production on earth is reaching its technological limits. In-orbit manufacturing can bring about an 88% increase in computational efficiency, as well as a 50% reduction in costs compared to production on Earth. Space Forge’s technology is highly scalable and is expected to have enough manufacturing capacity to cover 5G networks in Germany and the UK in the next 5 years. The returnable satellite platform on its own is a technology with several sizable market-changing opportunities. The team: CEO Joshua Western has worked in the space industry for over a decade. He worked closely with key government and industry stakeholders at the beginning of his career at Thales Space and later at the UK Space Agency. Co-founder and CTO Andrew Bacon is a senior expert in designing and launching satellites. Since 2009, he has been working for industry leaders like Clyde Space, SEA and Thales. description: TreeCard is building a superapp for environmental consumers. The product provides users with a suite of fintech, lifestyle and ecommerce alternatives, allowing them to effortlessly live more sustainably responsible. TreeCard is now expanding across the US and worldwide.

description: Munich-based aircraft manufacturer VÆRIDION is developing a zero-emission electric Microliner that is on track to deliver affordable regional flights in Europe by 2030 . VÆRIDION is the first e-aviation company to have secured a milestone Pre-Application Contract (PAC) with the EASA – a highly significant achievement that confirms VÆRIDION’s Microliner meets certification standards for commercial passenger aircraft, and puts the company ahead of competitors. Their patented prototype Microliner will start as a nine-seater aircraft. The Microliner has a nominal range of 400 km plus IFR reserves, has already passed initial functional and validation tests, and has prototype flights set to take off in 2027. The company has plans in place to scale the technology to long-term offer pan-European flights. The Microliner is a fixed-wing aircraft with advanced battery-wing integration and multi-engine single propeller configuration, all designed for maximum safety and efficiency. It emits less noise than conventional aircraft, making it well-suited to smaller airfields and easy to roll out in underserved areas. Delivered at scale, it would help drive economic growth and accessibility. Europe is currently nowhere near reaching its sustainable aviation goals, and the Microliner presents a long-term solution. VÆRIDION has already signed its first customers in Denmark (Copenhagen AirTaxi and Copenhagen Helicopter), Benelux (ASL Group) and Germany (Aero-Dienst). The Microliner will initially serve business passengers before expanding into consumer travel. The company already wields a world-class team made up of 38 aerospace, software and automotive experts, and partnerships with institutions including TU Munich and Bauhaus Luftfahrt e.V. In 2024, VÆRIDION also opened a state-of-the-art battery development facility at the Bosch Collaboration Campus and launched a Dutch subsidiary, which will allow VÆRIDION to leverage the innovation ecosystem surrounding TU Delft and accelerate the journey to commercialisation. VÆRIDION is also exploring applications for the aircraft in air ambulance services in collaboration with Aero-Dienst, which operates a fleet on behalf of ADAC.
